_what: Model-free retrieval acceptance fixture: which externally-named implementer symbols does CE's per-element retrieval put in front of the selection model for US 8,752,101 claim 1 x ExoPlayer3? Proposed by asus-CC (#311, 2026-09-04) after scoring CE's charts against an independent ChatGPT reference chart: all 14 of its cited symbols are IN the index, and CE reached one family of them.
_note_reachable_is_not_cited: This fixture measures whether retrieval puts a symbol in the selected target list, NOT whether the analysis model then cites it. Conflating those would let a merge-rule change take credit for a retrieval property (asus-CC, #311).
element_words_provenance: RUN 17's recorded per-element predicted words (asus-CC, #311 comment of 2026-09-04, claude vocabulary step at temp 0). Pinned so the test runs the SEARCH half of retrievePerElement with no model call. Cloud temp-0 drift means a live run's words differ slightly run to run; the pinned set is one honest draw, held constant so reachability deltas measure the SEARCH mechanism, not vocabulary variance.

sources_legend.chatgpt-external: RMS_ChatGPT_ExoPlayer3_claim_chart.txt — written at a prospective customer's request from knowledge of ExoPlayer, with no exposure to this project's priors. The external, independent list.
sources_legend.asus-reading: asus-CC's own regex of believed implementers, written from its reading of ExoPlayer ~10 days before the ChatGPT chart existed (#311). NOT independent of this project — asus-CC had read CE's ExoPlayer output for weeks — which is why the intersection with chatgpt-external is the strongest evidence tier: two sources, no contact, same answer.

_contamination_note: shouldStartPlayback appears twice in HANDOVER_TO_ASUS_CC_080926_1114am.md, written TO asus-CC before its reading began, so its asus-reading provenance is inherited, not independent (asus-CC's own provenance audit, #311). It is excluded from the independent intersection count.

ratchet._rule: REPORT + RATCHET: the test reports N-of-M reachable per set and FAILS only when a count falls below its floor. Floors are the recorded high-water marks — raise them (in this file, with a dated note) when a retrieval change legitimately lifts a count; never lower them without a population-justified, disclosed reason. A floor rise accompanied by a re-pin of element_words measures VOCABULARY, not search — the pinned words hold vocabulary constant within the test, so repinning them to a better temp-0 draw can raise every count with no search-mechanism change (asus-CC, #311). Re-pins must add their own dated history entry with a fresh words_pinned_at, so the diff shows the words moved.

history.note: Initial baseline at a80c6b1, measured through the full default selection stack (per-element round-robin depth 3 + content-arm promoted slot + concentration + drilldown + whole-claim arm). One family reached: AdaptiveTrackSelection + updateSelectedTrack, via the content arm's promoted slot on element 6. Agrees with asus-CC's independent ad-hoc measurement (1 family of 14, #311).

_single_pairing_caveat: A fixture becomes a target: a number that can only be chased on one claim is worse than no number (asus-CC, #311). A second pairing (Sonos 9,195,258 x ExoPlayer3 is the named candidate; the 385-claim corpus can supply more) should join this file's format in its own fixture before anyone tunes retrieval against these floors.
